newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank repeats call for lower rates.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank repeats call for lower rates.

text.p: Bank of Thailand governor Rerngchai Marakanond said Tuesday commercial banks should quickly cut lending rates to help boost the sagging economy.
"Commercial banks should speed up their cuts of interest rates because sustained high rates will further hurt the slowing economy," Rerngchai told reporters.
"This (the slowing economy) will eventually have an adverse impact on most banks themselves," he added.
Rerngchai urged that Thai prime lending rates, especially the Minimum Lending Rate (MLR), be cut in line with those made by commercial banks on deposit rates earlier this year.
"Deposit rates have already declined 1-1.5 percentage points while lending rates have been cut only 0.25 point," he said.
Current Thai MLR stands at 13.25-13.75 percent.
The governor said recent increased and stable money market liquidity is a positive factor that should induce banks to cut lending rates.
Private economists project that the Thai economy will expand at a 10-year low rate of six to seven percent this year against 8.6 percent growth in 1995.
